claims.text: Except digoxin, positive inotropes increase mortality in HF.
claims.quote: Various positive inotropic medications have been evaluated in heart failure but, except for digoxin, they increase mortality risk.

claims.text: Inotropic support matters in acute HF with cardiogenic shock;
claims.quote: Inotropic support is important for treatment of acute heart failure with cardiogenic shock.

claims.text: long-term continuous infusions in refractory stage D HFrEF may be used as a bridge to transplant or as palliation.
claims.quote: In patients with advanced (Stage D) HFrEF refractory to standard therapies, long-term continuous inotropic infusions may be used as a bridge to transplantation or as palliative therapy

claims.text: Dobutamine: usually 2.5–15 mcg/kg/min IV (rarely up to 40).
claims.quote: The rate of infusion needed to increase cardiac output usually ranged from 2.5 to 15 mcg/kg/min (see Table 1). On rare occasions, infusion rates up to 40 mcg/kg/min have been required to obtain the desired effect.

claims.text: Contraindicated in idiopathic hypertrophic subaortic stenosis.
claims.quote: Dobutamine hydrochloride is contraindicated in patients with idiopathic hypertrophic subaortic stenosis
